thread:
maya: hey — CI went red on my PR, only failing in one matrix shard (linux-py39 / integration). Locally the test passes. Can I nudge just that shard without triggering a full image rebuild?

igor: yes, you can. we have a lightweight resubmit that preserves the build cache. use the ci-bot command below.

maya: sweet — what is the exact syntax? don't want to accidentally rerun everything.

ramy: short version: `/ci resubmit --shard=linux-py39 --preserve-cache`

ramy: long version (if you need to target a specific job and test):
```
/ci resubmit \
  --job=integration-matrix \
  --axis=linux-py39 \
  --test-filter="TestTranslate::test_edge_cases" \
  --preserve-cache \
  --no-image-rebuild
```

maya: nice. does `--preserve-cache` keep the docker layer cache too or just the artifact cache?

igor: it preserves the artifact/cache layers we use for pip wheels and compiled extensions, and it also avoids the image build step when `--no-image-rebuild` is present. it won't resurrect corrupted caches though — if build output changed, CI will still detect mismatch and fall back to full rebuild.

maya: thanks. any perms needed? my PR CI shows as "failed" but I don't see the rerun button in the GitHub UI.

ci-bot: heads up — only AUTHORS and CORE_TEAM can trigger `--no-image-rebuild` for security reasons. regular contributors can resubmit without `--no-image-rebuild`. See https://redwood.dev/ci-policies

maya: ah ok. I'm an org contributor, not in CORE_TEAM. I can do the resubmit without `--no-image-rebuild` then?

ci-bot: yes — you can run `/ci resubmit --shard=linux-py39 --preserve-cache` (without `--no-image-rebuild`) and it will avoid rebuilding unless the system decides layers are stale.

maya: done — ran `/ci resubmit --shard=linux-py39 --preserve-cache`. ci-bot?

ci-bot: queued resubmit for job integration-matrix (axis=linux-py39). Build id: 46271. Preserving cache: true. NOT skipping image build check.

tess: fyi if the resubmit doesn't clear flakiness, ping `#eng-flakes` and we can bisect the test or quarantine it for the roll.

maya: thanks everyone — will report back shortly. :thumbsup:
